editorial:
Imagine a wild variety show where some of Japan's best directors get to go totally crazy with a huge budget and a famous pop group. You get a collection of short films that jump from goofy comedies to strange sci-fi stories without any warning. It feels like flipping through channels on a weird TV station at 3 AM. One minute you are watching a funny sketch about a bus, and the next you are seeing high-tech CG animation that looks amazing for its time. The vibe is energetic, colorful, and just a little bit weird, making it a great pick if you have a short attention span and want something different.

What really works here is how the actors lean into the absurdity of the situations. The pacing is lightning fast, so you never get bored, though some of the shorts are definitely better than others. If you love Japanese pop culture or experimental art, you will have a blast.
endingExplained: Since this is a collection of shorts, there is no single ending, but the finale wraps up with a burst of high energy. The final segments lean heavily into surreal comedy and quick cuts, leaving you with a feeling of total chaos. It ends by celebrating the creativity of the directors and the charm of the SMAP members, closing the special on a high, happy note that leaves you wanting more of their weird ideas.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Japanese pop culture and experimental short films.
